title: Елена в гостях у Баринова  (Elena Visits Barinov's Place)

segments.t: Welcoming Elena Pavlovna into Lyova's modest apartment, Chef Barinov claims that he shares the flat with his elderly mother and a struggling friend he generously took in. Deeply moved by his apparent kindness, Elena apologizes for misjudging him and leans in closer.
Какой вы благородный человек, Александр Петрович.
Да, так заботится о маме, о друге.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'I told him.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'to say' without extra filler words.
'Let him stay with us for a while.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'let' before landing on 'us'.
Какой вы благородный человек, Александр Петрович.
'What a noble man you are, Viktor Petrovich.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'what' and finishing on 'Petrovich'. Lyova answers right away.
Да, так заботится о маме, о друге.
'Yes, taking such good care of your mother and your friend.' The meaning hinges on 'yes' working together with 'friend' in spoken Russian.
'While I.' In spoken Russian, a compact phrase like this carries the full meaning through tone and context.
'To tell you the truth.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'fair' and finishing on 'speaking'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Please forgive me.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'forgive' and 'me' in a few short words.
'It is nothing, think nothing of it.' The meaning hinges on 'nothing' working together with 'nothing' in spoken Russian.
'What kind of man I should not be.' Notice how Russian expresses 'by what' and 'maybe' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Lyova answers right away.
'It turns out I did not know you at all.' The '-a' ending on the past-tense verb for 'knew' marks a female speaker or subject.
'Then let us get to know each other much better.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'like this' before landing on 'closer'.
'Excuse me, I...' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'excuse me' before landing on 'I'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Now we can get acquainted.' The meaning hinges on 'can' working together with 'get acquainted' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Какой вы благородный человек, Александр Петрович.
Да, так заботится о маме, о друге.

That wraps up this scene as at Lyova's apartment, Chef Barinov tells Elena Pavlovna that the room belongs to his mother and a struggling friend he took in, charming her with his apparent nobility. Until next time!
